questions.stem: A 68-year-old man presents with crushing central chest pain for 40 minutes. ECG shows ST elevation in leads II, III and aVF. Which coronary artery is most likely occluded?
questions.explanation: ST elevation in II, III and aVF is an inferior MI, most often from the right coronary artery. LAD occlusion gives anterior changes (V1-V4).

questions.stem: A 72-year-old woman with heart failure has breathlessness and ankle swelling. Which drug is most appropriate for rapid relief of fluid overload?
questions.explanation: Loop diuretics relieve congestion. Beta blockers and ACE inhibitors improve prognosis but do not treat fluid overload quickly.

questions.stem: A 24-year-old man has polyuria, polydipsia and weight loss over 3 weeks. Blood glucose is 28 mmol/L and ketones are 4.2 mmol/L. What is the most appropriate initial management?
options: IV fluids followed by a fixed-rate IV insulin infusion
questions.explanation: This is diabetic ketoacidosis. First-line management is IV fluids then a fixed-rate IV insulin infusion with potassium monitoring. Bicarbonate is not routine.

questions.stem: A 55-year-old man has a 3-day history of fever, productive cough and right-sided pleuritic chest pain. CXR shows right lower lobe consolidation. Which organism is the most common cause?
questions.explanation: Streptococcus pneumoniae is the commonest cause of community-acquired pneumonia. Klebsiella and Pseudomonas are more typical in alcoholics and structural lung disease respectively.

questions.stem: A 30-year-old woman presents with weight loss, palpitations, heat intolerance and a diffuse goitre with exophthalmos. Which antibody is most likely to be positive?
questions.explanation: Graves' disease is caused by stimulating TSH receptor antibodies. Exophthalmos is specific to Graves'.

questions.stem: A 45-year-old man presents with sudden severe headache described as 'a blow to the back of the head'. CT head is normal 8 hours after onset. What is the next best step?
options: Lumbar puncture at least 12 hours after onset
questions.explanation: Suspected subarachnoid haemorrhage with a normal CT after 6 hours needs lumbar puncture (at least 12 hours from onset) looking for xanthochromia.

questions.stem: A 60-year-old man on warfarin for atrial fibrillation presents with a significant GI bleed and an INR of 8.0. Which is the most appropriate reversal?
options: Prothrombin complex concentrate plus IV vitamin K
questions.explanation: Major bleeding on warfarin is treated with prothrombin complex concentrate plus IV vitamin K. Protamine reverses heparin.

questions.stem: A 28-year-old woman has episodes of fatigue, joint pain and a facial rash worsened by sunlight. Which test is most specific for her likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: This is SLE. ANA is sensitive but not specific. Anti-dsDNA and anti-Smith are the specific antibodies.

questions.stem: A 50-year-old alcoholic man presents with confusion, ataxia and ophthalmoplegia. What is the most appropriate immediate treatment?
questions.explanation: This is Wernicke's encephalopathy. Give IV high-dose thiamine immediately, before glucose, which could precipitate worsening.

questions.stem: A 65-year-old smoker has haemoptysis, hypercalcaemia and a central lung mass on CXR. What is the most likely histological type?
questions.explanation: Squamous cell carcinoma is central and causes hypercalcaemia via PTHrP. Adenocarcinoma is peripheral. Small cell causes SIADH and ACTH.

questions.stem: A 35-year-old woman has epigastric pain relieved by eating. Urea breath test is positive. Which is the most appropriate first-line eradication therapy?
options: PPI, amoxicillin and clarithromycin (or metronidazole) for 7 days
questions.explanation: H. pylori eradication is triple therapy: a PPI with two antibiotics, usually amoxicillin plus clarithromycin or metronidazole, for 7 days.

questions.stem: A 70-year-old man has a resting tremor, bradykinesia and cogwheel rigidity. Degeneration of neurons in which structure is responsible?
questions.explanation: Parkinson's disease results from loss of dopaminergic neurons in the substantia nigra pars compacta. Caudate degeneration is Huntington's.
